walkthroughs.body_html:
Christianity: Beliefs, Marriage & the Family, Living the Christian Life, Matters of Life & Death (Spec A) — a core area of GCSE Religious Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Christianity: Beliefs, Marriage & the Family, Living the Christian Life, Matters of Life & Death (Spec A) brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Christianity: Beliefs, Marriage & the Family, Living the Christian Life, Matters of Life & Death (Spec A).

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: When was the Trinity affirmed by council?
options: AD 33
AD 325

mcqs.q: Who developed the doctrine of original sin?
options: Aquinas
Augustine
Luther
Calvin

mcqs.q: What is the doctrine of the Trinity?
options: Christians believe everyone is reincarnated until they accept Jesus.
God is one being existing in three persons (Father, Son, Holy Spirit) — distinct in person but united in essence; Christians remain monotheistic.
Christians believe in three different gods.
The Trinity refers to heaven, earth and hell.

mcqs.q: What do Christians mean by resurrection, and how does it differ from reincarnation?
options: Christians believe everyone is reincarnated until they accept Jesus.
The Trinity refers to heaven, earth and hell.

Resurrection is the once-for-all bodily raising to eternal life at the end of time (modelled on Christ's resurrection); reincarnation is the soul's repeated rebirth into new bodies. They are distinct doctrines from different religious traditions.
Resurrection and reincarnation are basically the same idea of life after death.

mcqs.q: What are the main Christian theories of atonement?
options: Atonement means Jesus apologised to humans for being born divine.
All Christians believe Jesus died only to pay God back for sin.
Christians believe everyone is reincarnated until they accept Jesus.

Penal substitution (Christ bore the punishment for sin), Christus Victor (Christ defeated evil powers through the cross), ransom theory (Christ paid a price to free humanity), and moral exemplar (Christ's death inspires love). Different traditions emphasise different theories.
